THE ISSUES & THE SOURCES

Religious liberty in Texas
and the United States.

A starting point for following religious freedom, constitutional rights, legislation, and the public debate.

What this site follows

Religious liberty questions reach beyond worship services. They arise in education, public benefits, professional licensing, employment, land use, and the treatment of religious institutions. Texas Religious Liberty Watch brings together official legislative records and daily news coverage to make those developments easier to follow.

The focus extends across faiths. A proposed law affecting one religious community can raise questions relevant to others. The tracker identifies measures for closer examination; inclusion does not express support or opposition.

Texas legislation and state law

The bill tracker covers the 90th Regular Session of the Texas Legislature. It includes potentially relevant bills and proposed constitutional amendments, links to official text and history, and a personal watchlist. A filed proposal is not an enacted law. Review labels distinguish screened captions from reviewed text.

For the underlying Texas legal sources, start with Texas Constitution article I, section 6, and the Texas Religious Freedom Restoration Act, Civil Practice and Remedies Code chapter 110. The official text is the source to consult when evaluating a particular provision.

National developments

The First Amendment addresses both the free exercise of religion and governmental establishment of religion. Federal litigation and national policy debates can affect how religious liberty questions arise in Texas. The National Archives’ Bill of Rights transcript provides the constitutional text.

Our news watch gathers Texas and national headlines with publisher attribution and links to the coverage. Reporting, opinion, advocacy, proposed legislation, and court decisions are different kinds of sources. Read the underlying text and relevant decisions before drawing conclusions about legal effect.

Follow an issue from source to discussion

  1. Find a proposal in the bill tracker and read its official text.
  2. Save it to your browser’s watchlist and add private working notes.
  3. Use the news watch to follow related reporting and public debate.
  4. Check the linked official record for current legislative action.
